title: Give each Herdr coding agent its own Blaxel sandbox
summary: Run Codex, Claude Code, or OpenCode in independent Blaxel sandboxes from Herdr. Reconnect to tasks and bring changes back as reviewed Git patches.
body_markdown:
Blaxel's[Herdr plugin](https://github.com/blaxel-ai/herdr-blaxel-sandbox-plugin) gives each coding task its own cloud sandbox. Run Codex, Claude Code, or OpenCode from Herdr, let the agent work on a remote copy of your project, and decide when its changes come back to your local repository.


That separation matters when several tasks are moving at once. One agent can change a dependency or rewrite a function while another explores a different part of the project. Each has its own files and running processes. Your local worktree stays available for your work and the changes you choose to import.


Consider an invoice dashboard with two changes in flight: currency formatting and sorting invoices by date. We ran each task with Codex in its own Blaxel sandbox, then reviewed the results before bringing a change back.


## 1. Give each task its own environment


Start from the project's worktree in Herdr. The plugin creates a sandbox, uploads a filtered snapshot, and opens the coding agent in a connected pane. A second Start creates another independent sandbox, even from the same worktree.


The dashboard keeps both environments visible. You can see which repository and branch each came from, which agent it runs, and its current state.


*Two tasks, two sandboxes, one local project to review against.*


The plugin filters the upload for ignored files, dependencies, environment files, common credential paths, and recognized secret patterns. It also keeps host coding-agent login files out of the snapshot. The[configuration reference](https://github.com/blaxel-ai/herdr-blaxel-sandbox-plugin/blob/main/docs/configuration.md) explains agent authentication and upload settings.


## 2. Inspect the work where it runs


In the formatting sandbox, Codex changed the amount display from` $1249.5` to` $1,249.50` and added tests for zero, cents, thousands, and refunds. The sorting task worked on its own copy of the same source file.


*The formatting change is ready to review inside its sandbox.*


You can also inspect a running application through a private preview on a configured port. This preview shows the formatting change before it was imported locally; the sorting task's edits belong to the other sandbox.


*Check the updated amounts in the running application before importing the patch.*


To return to existing work, choose Reconnect. Start creates another environment. A local terminal disconnect leaves the remote session available to reconnect to, subject to the sandbox's lifecycle policy.


## 3. Choose what reaches your repository


When you're ready to bring a result back, select its sandbox in the dashboard and choose Apply. The plugin exports a Git patch, checks it against your current local worktree, and shows a summary before asking for approval.


*Review the proposed files before approving the import.*


After approval, the plugin checks the patch again before applying it. We imported the formatting change and reran its four tests locally; all passed. The sorting change stayed in its own sandbox.


Separate environments let agents work independently, but combining their edits still needs review. A conflicting patch stops the import. A patch that applies cleanly still needs the tests and code review you'd give any other change.


## Try it with one task


Follow the[plugin quick start](https://github.com/blaxel-ai/herdr-blaxel-sandbox-plugin#quick-start) to install it in Herdr and launch an agent. Choose one change, inspect its result in Blaxel, and bring back the patch when you're ready.


Keep work you need before deleting a sandbox or letting its configured idle-deletion policy expire. Stop preserves its files; Delete removes the environment.
